name: Pharaoh
description: Pharaoh living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: The Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

points: Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmaelites. And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; his master saw that the Lord was with him, and made him overseer over his house.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: The interpretation came to pass on the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday: the chief butler was restored, and the chief baker was hanged, as Joseph had interpreted. Wherever you read of Pharaoh's birthday or Herod's birthday, something bad always happens. We never celebrated birthdays; it's a day of proclaiming yourself to be God.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: On the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, it happened just as Joseph laid it out: the chief butler was restored unto his butlership again, and the chief baker was hanged.

note.label: Genesis 40: Do Not Interpretations Belong to God

points: His spirit was troubled, and none of the magicians and wise men of Egypt could interpret the dreams unto Pharaoh.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

points: Pharaoh told Joseph he had heard he could understand a dream to interpret it, and Joseph gave all the praise to the Most High: it is not in me; God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

points: Verse 1 says at the end of two full years; it's not telling you how long Joseph was in prison altogether. Joseph answered Pharaoh, it is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: The dream is one: seven years of great plenty, and after them seven years of famine; and for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice, it is because the thing is established by God. That famine shall surely happen.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: The dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice because the thing is established by God, and God will surely bring it to pass.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

points: Pharaoh said, can we find such a one as this, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? He took off his ring and put it upon Joseph's hand, arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, made him to ride in the second chariot, and they cried before him, bow the knee. We're going to tell the nations that too: bow the knee.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: Pharaoh set Joseph over his house and over all the land of Egypt; only in the throne was Pharaoh greater. Without Joseph no man lifted up his hand or foot in all Egypt: nothing moved unless Joseph decreed it.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

points: In the video Price points to Joseph marrying an Egyptian woman. Pharaoh gave Joseph Asenath, the daughter of Potipherah priest of On, and she bare him Manasseh and Ephraim before the years of famine came.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah and gave him Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On to wife. These heathens always like to change our names; that is one reason America is called spiritual Egypt, because they do the same thing that ancient Egypt did.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

points: Joseph was 30 years old when he stood before Pharaoh. He went in at 17; he was 13 years in prison and servitude, and came out at 30.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and his sons carried him and their little ones and their wives in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent, and all his seed came with him into Egypt.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: Naming their trade set Israel apart in Goshen, which was fertile land, and the favor Joseph had was bestowed upon him through Pharaoh to give them that land.

note.label: Genesis 46: Israel Comes into Egypt, Threescore and Ten Souls

points: Joseph took five of his brethren and presented them unto Pharaoh, and they answered as Joseph instructed: thy servants are shepherds, both we and also our fathers; for to sojourn in the land are we come. The Hyksos history is why that answer secured them Goshen.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: Joseph gave the people seed and made it a law over Egypt: give the fifth part unto Pharaoh, and four parts are your own for seed of the field, for your food, and for your households and little ones.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

points: When Jacob died, Pharaoh gave Joseph leave to bury his father, and the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of Egypt, and all the house of Joseph and his brethren went up together, a very great company, and mourned seven days at the threshing floor of Atad.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: All the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with Joseph and his brethren and his father's house, with chariots and horsemen, a very great company.

note.label: Genesis 50: The Burial of Jacob and the Forgiveness of Joseph

points: The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house.
